newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar's al-Khaleej oil field goes onstream.
newsitem.headline: Qatar's al-Khaleej oil field goes onstream.

text.p: A new offshore oilfield in Qatar operated by a subsidiary of France's Elf Aquitane went onstream on Saturday, industry sources said.
They said al-Khaleej field, operated by Elf Petroleum Qatar, will initially produce 20,000 barrels per day (bpd), rising gradually to 30,000 bpd by the year-end.
The field, covering an area of 2,837 sq km (1,108 sq miles), was discovered by Elf in 1990, but production has been delayed due to financial and technical difficulties.

The concession is now jointly held by a consortium comprising Elf Aquitaine, 55 percent, and Italy's Agip, 45 percent, under a 25-year production-sharing agreement with the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC).
Al-Khaleej's start-up lifts the gas-rich state's oil production capacity to close to 600,000 bpd. Qatar is the smallest producer in the 11-member Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

The field is one of six awarded by Qatar over the past three years to foreign companies under production-sharing agreements to boost the state's oil production capacity to more than 700,000 bpd by 2000.
Qatar's total oil reserves -- both onshore and offshore -- are estimated at around four billion barrels, QGPC sources said.
